text:
Ana (People Ops): Heads up — Diego M. just flagged his Feb paystub. Looks like payroll deducted German social security AND US FICA/401(k) for the same pay period. Can payroll + mobility review? Pay period 2024-02-01 — 2024-02-28.

Paystub snippet:
```text
Gross: EUR 8,500
Germany Sozialversicherung: EUR 1,020
401(k) pre-tax: USD 450 (converted)
US FICA: USD 520
Net: EUR 5,300
```
Link to stub: <https://payroll.redwood/secure/stubs/DiegoM/2024-02>
Diego's mobility note says assignment was short (<183 days). @Lena (GM) — can you confirm dates? :eyes:

Jin (Payroll): @Ana thanks. Was he coded onto DE payroll for pay date 2024-02-28 or was it a manual local levy? Need payrun id + global employee id to look up.

Marta (Payroll Ops): Payrun ID PR-20240228-42. Employee GID: RWF-4492. I can see DE payroll element `SOZ_DE` and US elements `FICA_US` + `401K_US`. Looks like a duplicate run for the same period — possibly a migration overlap.

payroll-bot: Ticket #PAY-9231 created: "Diego M - duplicate DE/US social contributions". Assigned to Marta. <https://payroll.redwood/tickets/PAY-9231>

Lena (Global Mobility): Confirmed — mobility docs show Diego returned 2024-02-02 and assignment end date recorded as 2024-01-31. Home contract stayed US. For a short secondment (<183 days) we should NOT have DE social for Feb. We'll need to support a refund reclaim.

Tom (Tax): Quick Q: do we have proof of <183 days (travel logs / badge)? Also need assignment letter. If Germany withheld employer+employee social, there are two routes: reclaim via employer payroll or have employee reclaim. We prefer employer reclaim so Diego isn't out-of-pocket.

Diego M.: Hi — I uploaded the assignment end memo and my travel logs to the mobility folder (Mobility/Diego_M/2024). I was back in SF on 02/01 and logged in from the office that day. Happy to share anything else.

Marta (Payroll Ops): Next steps from payroll side: 1) Reverse DE social elements in PR-20240228 and run a net pay adjustment for Feb (to restore Diego's net). 2) Reverse any 401(k) deferral recorded on the DE element if present and coordinate with Fidelity to correct deferral totals. 3) Prepare employer refund request to the DE authority (Bundesbank/Finanzamt process) + supporting payroll records. ETA: will aim to have reversals posted by EOW and begin reclaim docs early next week.

Ana (People Ops): Thank you. @Tom — does this mean we should expect a W-2 correction (W-2c) if FICA was withheld and then reversed after year-end processing? Also check HSA/401k limits impact.

Tom (Tax): If we can reverse FICA before year-end processing, we can avoid a W-2c. If reversal posts after W-2 is finalized, we will need W-2c. I'll monitor and confirm once Marta posts reversal. For DE refunds, payroll should retain employer proof; tax will assist with reclaim language.

Jin (Payroll): Noted. Marta, once you reverse the DE elements, please send me the journal entries so we can reconcile month close.

Marta (Payroll Ops): Will do. PR link: internal://payroll/pr/PR-20240228-42. I'm copying @Lena for the mobility docs. Diego — expect a DM about timing for the net adjustment. :thumbsup:

Lena (Global Mobility): I'll pull travel badge logs + assignment letter and send them to PAY-9231. I'll also contact our Berlin ER rep to confirm local reclaim steps.

payroll-bot: PAY-9231 status updated -> "in progress" (assigned: Marta).

Ana (People Ops): Summary/action owners: Marta — reverse runs + file DE refund; Lena — supply docs & local contact; Tom — confirm W-2 impact; Jin — reconcile journals after reversal. Diego, we'll keep you posted by EOW. Thanks all.
